tier_reason: Upgraded from C: the peer-reviewed QuickETC2 paper (ACM Trans. Graph. 39(6) Article 270, Dec 2020, by a third party) times etcpak 0.7 against Etc2Comp (effort=0) and ETCPACK 4.0.1 (the reference ETC2 encoder in Arm's Mali Texture Compression Tool) on 64 textures on a Ryzen 7 3700X under Ubuntu 20.04 with PSNR/SSIM reported. Not A: compiler and flags are not stated and the harness is only an ACM supplement (patch plus executables), not a public repo; the README's own numbers have no competitor timing.

corrections.baseline: Etc2Comp (effort=0, error metric rgba) and ETCPACK 4.0.1 (reference ETC2 encoder in Arm Mali Texture Compression Tool 4.3.0), as measured in the QuickETC2 paper (ACM TOG 2020); the current README only cites the NVIDIA in-driver ETC2 decoder (42.5 Mpx/s) for decompression, and the 2016-2018 README (etcpak 0.5) timed PVRTexToolCLI 3.5, Mali etcpack 4.2, etc2comp and crunch (rg-etc1) 1.04.
corrections.claimed_speedup: QuickETC2 paper Table 1 (Ryzen 7 3700X, fastest settings, 55 RGB textures): etcpak 0.7 ETC1 3250 Mpx/s and ETC2 planar-only 1931 Mpx/s (16 threads, SIMD) vs Etc2Comp ETC2 3.8 Mpx/s (16 threads) and ETCPACK ETC2 1.4 Mpx/s (single-threaded); with one thread and SIMD disabled, etcpak ETC1 44.6 and ETC2(p) 28.9 Mpx/s vs Etc2Comp 3.1 and ETCPACK 1.4 Mpx/s. Ratios (derived from page data): ETC2(p) about 508x vs Etc2Comp and 1379x vs ETCPACK at highest-performance settings, 9.3x and 20.6x single-thread scalar. Quality is lower: etcpak ETC2(p) 36.82 dB PSNR vs 37.89 dB (Etc2Comp) and 38.09 dB (ETCPACK); etcpak ETC1 35.87 dB. The paper's SIGGRAPH 2020 talk table gives etcpak 0.6.1 1782 Mpix/s vs Etc2Comp 4.0 and ETCPACK 1.3 Mpix/s. First-party README (Ryzen 9 7950X, 16K x 16K atlas): ETC1 797 Mpx/s ST / 9613 MT, ETC2 356/6378, BC1 5730/10174, BC3 2437/8568, BC7 12.1/225; ETC2 decode 599 Mpx/s ST vs 'Nvidia in-driver ETC2 decoder can do only 42.5 Mpx/s' (about 14x, derived from page data; no machine given for the NVIDIA figure). Historical README table (etcpak 0.5, 2016, Xeon E3-1230 v3, 8192x8192 RGB): etcpak 0.5 AVX2 ETC1 872.6 Mpx/s vs crunch (rg-etc1) 1.04 11.53, etc2comp effort=0 1.96, PVRTexToolCLI 3.5 1.3 (total time including image decode) and Mali etcpack 4.2 0.777 Mpx/s.
corrections.hardware: QuickETC2 paper: AMD Ryzen 7 3700X @3.6 GHz, 8 cores with SMT, 32 GB RAM, Ubuntu 20.04. README: AMD Ryzen 9 7950X, Intel i7 1185G7, Apple M3 Max (historical README: Intel Xeon E3-1230 v3).
corrections.workload: Paper: compression of 64 test textures (256x256 to 8192x8192; 55 RGB, 9 RGBA) with each encoder at its fastest setting, highest-performance (16 threads, SIMD) and baseline-control (1 thread, no SIMD) settings, PSNR and SSIM reported. README: ETC1, ETC2, BC1, BC3 and BC7 compression and decompression of a non-public real-life RGBA 16K x 16K atlas, single-threaded and multithreaded.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 331 stars, 50 forks; README says it is used in production builds by millions of users; the QuickETC2 paper says Unity integrated etcpak (alongside ETCPACK and Etc2Comp) since Unity 2017.3
corrections.caveats: Speed comes at lower quality: in the QuickETC2 paper etcpak's ETC2 mode is planar-only (no T- and H-modes at version 0.7), so it searches a smaller mode space than Etc2Comp and ETCPACK and scores about 1.1-1.3 dB lower PSNR; compare at matched quality before treating the ratios as like-for-like. In the paper's highest-performance setting ETCPACK ran single-threaded while etcpak used 16 threads; the single-thread scalar ratios (9.3x, 20.6x) are the fair algorithmic comparison. Compiler and flags are not stated anywhere; etcpak's CMakeLists.txt enables -march=native by default. The README's own benchmark (Application.cpp -b mode) uses a non-public atlas and times no competitor; the competitor table was removed from the README in 2018 and the NVIDIA decoder figure has no stated machine. The paper's numbers are for etcpak 0.7 / 0.6.1, not the current 2.1. BC1/BC3/BC7 speed claims have no competitor numbers.

notes: The search agent missed the independent evidence: the QuickETC2 paper PDF is reachable on raw.githubusercontent.com (nahjaeho.github.io repo) and gives etcpak vs Etc2Comp/ETCPACK speed and PSNR on a named CPU, so the entry moves C to B. Etc2Comp and ETCPACK/Mali tool are recognisable ETC incumbents; the win is real but at lower quality (planar-only ETC2, ~1 dB PSNR less). Aras Pranckevicius's 'Texture Compression in 2020' blog also covers etcpak but is blocked here (search snippet only, not used for the tier).

tier_reason: The numbers live only in the README 'Performance' section (added in commit 'Add performance stats', 2026-09-27): first-party wall times vs giflib 5.2.2 and stb_image, GCC 11.5 -O2 on Linux 6.4, but no CPU model and, as the author states, the harness is not published (tests/ holds only accuracy tests: run.sh, gif_test.c). Number without harness or CPU model is C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README tables (best of two runs, wall time in ms): warm cache, gif_load read() beats giflib 5.2.2 stream by 1.28x-1.72x and mmap() by 1.42x-1.78x (derived from page data; README says 1.3x-1.7x), and beats stb_image by 1.4x-2.5x per the README (derived from page data: 1.39x-2.42x for the +RGBA rows, which composite like stb_image), e.g. 1080p shapes 668 ms (read) vs giflib stream 1149 ms vs stb_image 1829 ms. Cold cache vs giflib stream: 1.3x-1.5x faster on the 3 shape GIFs (derived from page data: 1.42x-1.51x with read()) but slower on the 3 noise GIFs; the README states 0.83x-0.85x, while its own table gives 0.89x-0.91x with read() and 0.75x-0.79x with mmap() (derived from page data). Author says the 1.3x-1.5x cold claim also holds on real giphy GIFs (no numbers). Peak memory: one frame plus a 16 KB code table; at 1080p giflib slurp holds 296 MB and stb_image 1254-1611 MB, while giflib stream holds a single row and is lower than gif_load.
corrections.caveats: The README says 'take everything below with a grain of salt' and that the harness is not published, so the numbers are not reproducible from the repo; no CPU model is given (only RAM latency 128 ns, 8 GB/s sequential read, EXT4 cold read 342 MB/s); synthetic GIFs only; best of two runs; timing includes file acquisition. The README's cold-cache noise ratio (0.83x-0.85x) does not match its own table. Work is comparable only because the test GIFs are not interlaced: gif_load leaves deinterlacing to the caller while giflib DGifSlurp does it; the plain rows return palette indices, so only the +RGBA rows match stb_image's composited output. giflib stream uses less memory than gif_load. Recent fixes landed around the measurement: int32 overflow and null-palette fix (2026-09-27) and a 1-byte out-of-bounds read at GIF_EHDM (2026-10-01, after the numbers were published). Public-domain dedication (Unlicense text in gif_load.h): no patent grant.

notes: Numbers match the README tables; the warm-cache headline ratios check out, but the cold noise ratio in the prose (0.83x-0.85x) disagrees with the table (0.89x-0.91x read, 0.75x-0.79x mmap). giflib is a recognisable GIF incumbent, not in the category's listed baselines (libjpeg-turbo, libpng, libwebp, libavif), so baseline_in_list false is right. Metadata (Unlicense, 85 stars, last commit 2026-10-01, active) checked.

tier_reason: First-party README table on a named CPU (i7-7820HQ, single thread, best of 128) with public benchmark code (Src/main.cpp times Goofy, stb_dxt, rgbcx, icbc and rg_etc1 on 42 test images and averages PSNR and time), but compiler and flags are not stated, so not A; no independent measurement found.

corrections.workload: Single-thread compression of the repo's 42 test images (24 Kodak images, lena, baboon, monarch, peppers, sail, tulips, parrot_red, patterns, five PBR textures including a normal map, six Roblox images; list in Src/main.cpp), best of 128 runs per image, averaged speed (MP/s) and RGB-PSNR, each encoder at its fastest or lowest-quality setting.
corrections.caveats: Speed-quality trade, not equal quality: the compared encoders score about 3.8-4.6 dB higher RGB-PSNR (Goofy DXT1 37.02 dB vs 40.82-41.00 dB; Goofy ETC1 36.30 dB vs rg_etc1 40.87 dB), and Goofy's ETC1 output is restricted to the ETC1S subset, so it does less search work than rg_etc1. The harness (Src/main.cpp) calls icbc::init_dxt1(), rgbcx::encode_bc1_init() and rg_etc1::pack_etc1_block_init() inside every timed call, so those competitors' times include one-time table setup; the stb_dxt wrapper has no such call, so the 33x ratio vs stb_dxt is the cleanest. Compiler and flags are not stated (the repo ships a VS2017 Win64 CMake generator script and CI builds Release with MSVC, GCC and Clang, but the README does not say which build produced the table). test-results/ holds only keep_me.txt, so no raw result files are published. Not suited to normal maps per the README.

notes: All numbers and ratios match the README. stb_dxt, rgbcx (bc7enc), icbc and rg_etc1 are recognisable texture-encoder incumbents; baseline_in_list false is right since the category lists image codecs. Flag for enrichment: competitor init calls sit inside the timed loop in Src/main.cpp, which inflates the rgbcx, icbc and rg_etc1 ratios by an unknown amount.
